The electric chair has not been completely "gotten rid of" in the United States; rather, it was gradually phased out as a primary method [d9][d4]. Most states shifted to lethal injection in the late 20th and early 21st centuries, and Nebraska was the last state to use the electric chair as its sole method of execution until the Nebraska Supreme Court ruled it unconstitutional in February 2008 [d5][d6]. Nationally, no state other than Tennessee used the electric chair after 2013, and the last recorded execution by electric chair in the US took place in Tennessee in 2020 [d2][d10]. Some states still retain it as an option if an inmate chooses it or if lethal injection cannot be performed, and numerous dormant electric chairs remain in American prisons [d4][d10].
